problems: british-colonial-empire shares Q8680 and the Wikipedia title 'British Empire' with british-empire (sa-06). Kept as two states: this is the global aggregate 1706-1999, british-empire is the East India Company's India 1757-1858, and many Indian dossiers name british-empire as counterpart. Not merged.

The row is not the empire's whole area: its 1920 shape is 12.03 M km2 against the infobox 35.5 M km2; the six British-family rows alive in 1920 (this row, british-africa, commonwealth-of-australia, british-raj, british-gold-coast, kingdom-of-great-britain) sum to 36.77 M km2.

Overlaps: english-colonial-empire covers 1709-1712 as well (771 of 777 cells shared; treated as a hand-over of rows); Canada, Australia and New Zealand are carried as Dominion vassals (1867-1931, 1901-1942, 1907-1947) while the verdicts remove their cells from the direct shape; sub-colony dossiers (belize, british-honduras, guyana, jamaica, barbados) draw ground this row also draws.

Other dossiers should hold the matching events with roles reversed: canada, commonwealth-of-australia, new-zealand, aden-protectorate, bahrain, kuwait, qatar, trucial-states, kingdom-of-iraq, mosquito-kingdom, qajar-dynasty, pahlavi-dynasty, british-africa, british-mandate-for-palestine.

One free-text counterpart remains: 'Falkland Islands (previous holder not named on the page)' (1833; falkland-islands.json exists).

38 of 144 events are confidence 1: Cliopatria bookkeeping (row hand-overs) and the shapes' own frontier growth where no page read dates it. The Mosquito Coast is a vassal pair 1704-1861 (TE) although Cliopatria draws the shore as direct land in 1734-1787 and 1846-1852 and gives it to its Mosquito Kingdom row in 1853.

TE (Territorial evolution of the British Empire) was opened six times with different questions because the reading model would not return its tables verbatim in one pass; 13 of the 14 allowed pages were opened, none failed.
